title.narrative: Output 3.5. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement labour market programmes and employment services for transitions to decent work over the life course, with particular focus on young and older workers

description.narrative:
In 2020 and 2021, the Ukrainian State Employment Service (SES) defined and partially implemented a comprehensive institutional reform, including the introduction of a modern staff development programme, a new workflow, new services, and an adapted organizational structure.
At the local level, the SES has become the driving force for the implementation of local employment partnerships (LEPs). LEPs are a set of labour market interventions jointly identified and realised by local stakeholders (including social partners) under the leadership of the local employment office. Thanks to a financial contribution of the Government of Denmark, the ILO provided technical guidance for the design of the SES reform, including the preparation and administration of the staff development programme, the identification and introduction of new services, and the review of the organizational structure.
Comprehensive training materials on the multiple facets of the SES reform were handed over to a team of internal trainers within the SES. The digitalization of the training programme was also initiated, in partnership with other employment services from the region.
The ILO delivered a capacity development programme to selected SES offices on the LEP methodology and on activation policies. Thanks to a financial contribution of the Government of Denmark, the ILO supported the implementation of three local employment partnerships in Kherson and Rivne (Sarny and Mlyniv) in order to showcase how the model functions and to ensure the participation and contribution of the social partners in these pilots.
The capacity development programme relied significantly on the ILO's facilitation of peer-learning and triangular cooperation with other public employment services (SSTC).
